text:
mira: quick follow-up from the GQA/MQA RFC — wanted to capture the open concerns for query-merge safety and a small rollout plan.

sam: thanks, mir. can you list the exact failure modes we worried about? i sketched a test matrix earlier.

mira: sure. short list: 1) kv-cache misalignment when merged queries have differing key offsets, 2) silent token duplication due to partial merge, 3) backpressure spikes when a large group gets coalesced, 4) degradation for short-latency single-query paths.

jon: for kv-cache misalignment — is this mainly from mixed sequence-length batches or from different past_key_lengths?

mira: both, but the tricky case is mixed past_key_lengths + prefix caching. when a merged group reorders invocation offsets we accidentally read wrong slice.

lina: proposal: forbid merging when any request in the candidate set has nonzero prefix_offset or when past_key_length mismatch > 0. cheap check: compare header past_key_len.

sam: that would be conservative but simple. downside: reduces merge rate on long-prefix workloads. maybe we can allow merge if all past_key_len are equal and prefix_offset % kv_block_size == 0?

mira: exactly. we can encode a compatibility hash in the request meta: "kv_sig" = (past_key_len, prefix_offset // kv_block_size, attention_cfg). merge permitted only if kv_sig identical across group.

jon: sounds good. need a fast-hash (u64) and compare. microbenchmark shows cost < 30ns per request. fine.

lina: what about partial failures? e.g., we start merging and one kernel throws OOM or returns EAGAIN. fallback strategy?

mira: fallback rules: 1) if kernel fails deterministically (OOM/EAGAIN) we retry split: requeue as individual requests to safe kernel; 2) increment a per-kernel penalty score to reduce future routing to that kernel; 3) if failure rate > 5% for 1 minute, auto-disable grouped-merge on that node and route to single-query path.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout suggested: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback if latency P95 regresses > 10% or error rate increases > 0.5%.

sam: tests: unit tests for kv_sig equality, fuzz tests with random prefix lengths, and an integration test that runs mixed workload (chat + batch rerank) for 30m under load.

jon: add perf counters: merge_rate, merge_reject_reasons (kv_sig_mismatch, prefix_nonzero, backpressure), merged_group_size_hist. dashboards need those.

lina: also add an API change note: requests need optional header: "x-kv-meta": { "past_key_len":"<int>", "prefix_offset":"<int>", "attention_cfg":"fp16:causal" } — avoid required fields by defaulting to 0. docs + SDKs need update.

mira: agree. SDKs: python/ts will populate automatically for new runtime. fallback: if header missing, runtime assumes past_key_len=0 and prefix_offset=0.

sam: conservatively rejecting when header absent is safer, but will break some clients. defaulting to 0 seems better for backward compat. note in changelog.

mira: rollout tasks (quick):
- impl kv_sig + fast check (sam)
- unit + fuzz tests (sam, jon)
- add counters & dashboard (jon)
- SDK header plumbing + docs (lina)
- canary job + alert rules (ops)

lina: timeline? two weeks to canary?

mira: aim for 10 working days. let’s start with a feature branch + PR with flags: feature.gqa_merge = on, config.merge_window_ms = 3.

jon: small nit: merge_window_ms probably needs to be tunable per model/region. add into routing config.

mira: yes — default 3ms, model override allowed.

sam: one more: add a safety net in selector: if predicted benefit (tokens_saved * latency_gain) < 0.5ms * group_size then skip merge. avoids micro-optimizations that cost more.

mira: good call. we’ll add an estimator that uses recent per-token cost.

lina: ok — I’ll start SDK PR for header and changelog.

mira: thanks all. I’ll open the feature PR and assign tasks. cc @sam @jon @lina. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder: please link the RFC PR in this thread when ready.
